items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I know a friend of mine, Bill Colburn, who lived with Bunk quite a while

ctx.x: And the trouble with this is that a lot of critics will come back on that and say, well, Louis was an entertainer, he wasn't a musician. But I think that if one understands the New Orleans tradition, those two things were very close.

Yeah, the entertaining is a part of it. I know a friend of mine, Bill Colburn, who lived with Bunk quite a while, a lot longer than I did, would explain that Bunk would play anything for anybody if he knew the tune at all, and also try to play in a way that people like. It was Louis Prima, his motto, did the poor guy ever recover?
Well, he's in a convalescent home here now.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I remember my friend Bill Colburn asked Bunk

ctx.x: Yeah. But they'd gone together... Anyway, say, 10 years or so ago, quite a while back. Anyway, George Barquet's brother, Sheil, who wasn't as well-known as George, down here at least, had passed for white for years. I know Mineta says he met him once on Canal Street after he started passing, and he said, well, I like it better. I forget. I have that in some of the Mineta interviews. Some of that stuff I'll copy, too, later on, which is on tape. He likes it better. Mineta sort of, you know, he wasn't mad at him or…
